market_question: Will the US acquire part of Greenland in 2026?
reasoning: The US acquiring sovereignty or exclusive jurisdiction over any part of Greenland by end of 2026 faces immense political and legal hurdles. Both Denmark and Greenland have consistently rejected US ownership ideas, and no binding agreement or treaty for such a transfer appears remotely feasible in the short timeframe, even if Trump pressures. A lease of basing rights wouldn't meet the high bar of exclusive jurisdiction unless Denmark/Greenland cede all authority, which is extremely unlikely. I estimate true probability around 3%, far below the market's 13.5% implied by price.
evidence_points: Greenlandic and Danish governments have repeatedly stated the island is not for sale, with the Danish PM saying 'Greenland is not for sale' as recently as 2025.
The resolution requires a binding agreement or legal instrument, not just rhetoric or negotiation talks, making a quick deal very improbable.
Even expanded US military presence (e.g., Pituffik base) falls under existing agreements with shared sovereignty, not exclusive US control.
